cards.explanation: The answer is that very field. The man found the treasure, hid it again, and in his joy went and sold all he had and bought that field (Matthew 13:44). The field is what he bought, friends, and the treasure was in it.

The answer is False. The text says that in his joy he went and sold all he had and bought that field (Matthew 13:44). Gloomy just doesn't fit a man who does it in his joy. I bet his neighbors have questions.

The answer is True. When the merchant found one very precious pearl, he went away and sold all he had and bought it (Matthew 13:46). He'd been searching for fine pearls, and this one was worth everything he owned. That's a man who knows exactly what he's looking at, friends.

The answer is all kinds of fish. The net was cast into the sea and caught all kinds of fish (Matthew 13:47). A net doesn't check IDs at the door, friends. When it was full, the men pulled it ashore and sorted what was in it (Matthew 13:48).

The answer is good. The text says they sat down and sorted the good fish into containers, but threw the bad away (Matthew 13:48). Good and bad are the words the text uses, friends. Nothing about size, nothing about looks, just good and bad.

The answer is righteous. Jesus says the angels will come and separate the wicked from the righteous (Matthew 13:49). This is the part where the fishing picture explains itself, friends. The sorting on the shore matches what happens at the end of the age.

The answer is into the fiery furnace. Jesus says the angels will separate the wicked from the righteous and throw them into the fiery furnace, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth (Matthew 13:49-50). I think this is a heavy part, friends, and it's okay to say so. Jesus said it plainly, so we hear it plainly.

The answer is True. Jesus asks, "Have you understood all these things?" and they answer, "Yes" (Matthew 13:51). The text gives us their answer and nothing more. I'd say that's a pretty confident group after three parables in a row, friends.

The answer is new treasures as well as old. Jesus says a scribe discipled in the kingdom of heaven is like a homeowner who brings out of his storeroom new treasures as well as old (Matthew 13:52). Both kinds come out of the same storeroom, friends. New and old are both right there in the verse.
